correctness.rationale: Under the exact source hypotheses take one-dimensional H=H_1=C, K=C=C'=I, Lambda_1=(1/2)I, Theta_1=0, lambda_1=lambda_2=0, c_1=1/2. Original controlled frame bounds are A=B=1/4. The operator difference Lambda*Lambda-Theta*Theta=(1/4)I is positive, so its positive square root has norm 1/2||f|| and saturates the printed perturbation hypothesis, eta=sum_i c_i²=1/4. Source Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.1 claim positive lower bound (sqrt A-eta)²=(1/2-1/4)²=1/16, yet perturbed analysis energy is identically zero. This directly contradicts the stated theorem and avoids all domain, infinite summation or noncommutativity issues. The separate valid replacement in the package assumes DIRECT component-square-root differences and invokes l² Minkowski to derive norm error sqrt eta, with strict smallness (1-lambda_1)sqrt A>sqrt eta; no assertion that the old sqrt(operator-difference) condition alone implies this replacement.
